name: grill-options
about: A grilling question with its choices as cards: `--option "Q1 a: label | consequence"` (once per option, at least two; given for a question, it replaces its options; only on an open question), the recommendation then an option's id (refused otherwise, on a question asked, revised or given options in this command); a grilling's `--body FILE` / `--no-body`, the context its questions share. Warned, not refused: a reason over 200 characters, a reason whose first sentence holds a source (path:line, ADR, a D-number), a consequence over 160, more than four options, and a question over 300. The old four-part `--ask` keeps working with no options.

content:
In short

The loop writes Postgres; the graph is rebuilt from it.

argv: Where new terms live | When the system learns a new legal term, where is it saved first? | a | Today one save keeps every term and its history in one place; a graph-only term could not be traced or undone.
The legacy form | Keep the four parts? (a) yes; (b) no | (a) | It is how every grilling so far was asked.
Q1 a: In Postgres, then copied to the graph | one place to save, trace and undo; the graph follows
Q1 b: Only in the graph | quicker to query, but nothing records who added it

Who checks a term | Should a person approve each new term before it is saved? | b | ADR-0024 says terms are saved as rows (ontology/pass-ontology.ts:512-584). A person approving each one would slow every pass, and the record keeps who added it so a bad term can be undone later; this reason runs on past two hundred characters on purpose.
Q3 a: A person approves each | slower, every term checked

Q3 b: Saved at once, undone if wrong | the fleet keeps going and a wrong term is found later by the review, then undone from its record, with the passes that used it run again from the record at a cost
Q2: D27 settled it. It still holds.
Q2 a: Yes | the old form stays
Q2 b: No | every ask gives options
Q2: The legacy form | Keep the four parts? | a | It is how every grilling so far was asked.
Q2 a: Yes | the old form stays
Q2 b: No | every ask gives options
Q2: The legacy form | Keep them? | yes | w
